claims.text: The initial material is a solution-annealed, equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA without solid-lubricant phases.
The intervention incorporates 5 vol% h-BN nanoparticles into the HEA by powder-metallurgy blending and hot consolidation.
Powder-metallurgy blending and hot consolidation will produce a uniform dispersion of the h-BN nanoparticles.
Sliding of the h-BN-modified HEA will form an h-BN-rich tribofilm at the interface.
The resulting tribofilm will have a lamellar structure.
Weak van der Waals bonding allows h-BN layers to shear easily under load and sliding.
Easy shear within the h-BN-rich tribofilm lowers interfacial shear and friction.
The h-BN-rich tribofilm prevents direct metal-metal contact.
Protection from direct contact reduces substrate material removal and wear.
Adding 5 vol% h-BN will reduce steady-state coefficient of friction by at least 30% relative to untreated CoCrFeMnNi.
Adding 5 vol% h-BN will reduce wear rate by at least 50% relative to untreated CoCrFeMnNi.
The predicted friction and wear reductions will hold from 25 to 600 °C during dry sliding at 5–20 N, 0.1–1 m/s, and relative humidity no greater than 30%.
The lubricating effectiveness of h-BN is expected to persist up to 600 °C.
Above approximately 600 °C, h-BN may oxidize to B2O3.
Oxidation of h-BN to B2O3 may degrade the lubricating tribofilm.
The stability and integrity of the h-BN tribofilm between 400 and 600 °C under humid conditions are not well established.

contradictions.description: The central prediction requires at least 30% friction reduction and 50% wear reduction across 25–600 °C, whereas the falsification rule uses only a 20% threshold and requires failure at at least three of four temperatures. Results could violate the stated prediction—for example, 25% friction and 40% wear reductions at every temperature—without satisfying the proposed falsification rule.
